The ''' 1943 [[German football championship]]''', the 36th edition of the competition, was won by [[Dresdner SC]], the club's first-ever championship, won by defeating [[FV Saarbrücken]] in the final.<ref name="List" >[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html (West) Germany -List of champions] rsssf.org, accessed: 26 December 2015</ref><ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/dresdner-sc/1/ Dresdner SC » Steckbrief] {{in lang|de}} Weltfussball.de – Dresdner SC honours, accessed: 26 December 2015</ref>

The twenty-nine [[1942–43 Gauliga|1942–43]] [[Gauliga]] champions, four more than in the previous season,<ref name="ReferenceA">''kicker Allmanach 1990'', page: 243-245</ref> competed in a single-leg knock out competition to determine the national champion.<ref name="Rsssf" >[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html German championship 1943] rsssf.org, accessed: 26 December 2015</ref> In the following season, the last completed one during the war, the German championship was played with thirty one clubs, expanded through a combination of territorial expansion of [[Nazi Germany]] and the sub-dividing of the Gauligas in later years.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>

The 1943 championship marked the end of the golden era of [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] which had reached the semi-finals of each edition of the national championship from 1932 to 1942 and won the competition in 1934, 1935, 1937, 1939, 1940 and 1942 while losing the final in 1933, 1938 and 1941. In 1943 defending champions Schalke was knocked out in the quarter-finals by [[Holstein Kiel]], thereby ending the clubs quest for a twelfth consecutive semi-finals appearance.<ref name="List" /><ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/fc-schalke-04/1/ FC Schalke 04 » Steckbrief] {{in lang|de}} Weltfussball.de – FC Schalke 04 honours, accessed: 26 December 2015</ref>

[[Ernst Kalwitzki]] of FC Schalke 04 and [[Herbert Binkert]] of [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] were the joint top scorers for the 1943 championship with five goals each, the lowest for any top scorer since 1925. For Kalwitzki it was the third and last time, after 1937 and 1939, to finish as top scorer.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 2 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

Dresdner SC became the last club to be awarded the ''[[Viktoria (trophy)|Viktoria]]'', the annual trophy for the German champions from 1903 to 1944. The trophy disappeared during the final stages of the war, did not resurface until after the [[German reunification]] and was put on display at the DFB headquarters in [[Frankfurt]] until 2015, when it was moved to the new ''[[Deutsches Fußballmuseum]]'' in [[Dortmund]].<ref>[https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/pokale-auf-reisen-viktoria-und-co-wandern-ins-fussballmuseum-123277/ POKALE AUF REISEN: VIKTORIA UND CO. WANDERN INS FUSSBALLMUSEUM] {{in lang|de}} DFB website, accessed: 27 December 2015</ref>

Dresdner SC completed the 1942–43 season unbeaten, finishing the [[Gauliga Sachsen]] with 18 wins out of 18 games, and winning all five games in the championship to claim the title.<ref name="Rsssf" /><ref>[http://www.f-archiv.de Das Deutsche Fussball-Archiv] {{in lang|de}} Historic German league tables, accessed: 29 December 2015</ref>

* Gauliga champions [[LSV Adler Deblin]] were replaced by [[SG Warschau]].
* Stuttgarter Kickers and VfB Stuttgart finished on equal points and the same goal average and were therefore declared joint champions but only VfB advanced to the German championship.
